title: Customers who have placed orders
statement_markdown: Return the names of customers who have at least one order. Do not duplicate a customer with several orders. Sort by name.

examples.explanation: This output comes from the visible sample data.

hints: You only need to test whether a matching order exists.
Use a correlated EXISTS subquery that links orders.customer_id to the current customer.
explanation: EXISTS returns true as soon as a matching order is found, so each customer appears once without DISTINCT. The inner query is correlated through customer_id. A common mistake is forgetting that link, which makes every customer pass when any order exists. An inner join with DISTINCT is an alternative.
reference_solution: SELECT name FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id) ORDER BY name

validation.setup_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR(50)); CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, amount INT); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'A'), (2, 'B'), (3, 'C'), (4, 'D'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1, 1, 100), (2, 1, 200), (3, 3, 150);
